_about: How Amass finds the identity provider behind a domain. The registered domain and each of its names whose first label is one of login_labels (stored names only; none are guessed) are asked for their OpenID Connect discovery document at oidc_path (OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0, oidc_source); its issuer is the host the domain's users sign in at (FQDN identity_provider). Microsoft's realm answer gives the same for a federated tenant (its AuthURL). A host under one of a provider's suffixes is that provider's tenant host, a third party of the domain; a provider with a tenant_path is asked there for its organization identifier (Okta's well-known organization metadata), stored as an Identifier of tenant_type that the domain's identity_tenant points at. Any other provider host is the organization's own federation server: its SAML/WS-Federation metadata at federation_metadata_path (federation_source) names the certificates that sign its tokens, stored as TLSCertificates (signing_certificate). At most max_hosts names of one registered domain are asked.
